facts.text: Scope is the stateful handle of one connected PicoScope 5000A device; it keeps the handle, the resolution, max_adc, the variant and serial strings and the configured channels
The clone targets the PicoScope 5000A/B series and was verified on a 5442B
The README describes a lean MCP server for PicoScope 5000A USB oscilloscopes developed and verified on a 5442B
connect opens the unit, reads max_adc with ps5000aMaximumValue and reads the variant and serial with ps5000aGetUnitInfo
The resolution must be one of 8, 12, 14, 15 and 16 bits
The channel names are A, B, C and D
set_channel validates the channel, maps AC or DC to PS5000A_AC or PS5000A_DC, picks the smallest range in _RANGE_NAMES that covers the request and calls ps5000aSetChannel
The full-scale voltage ranges run from 0.01 V to 20.0 V
set_channel defaults to enabled=True, coupling='DC', range_volts=5.0 and analog_offset=0.0
The README states that set_channel covers channel A to D, enable, DC/AC and a range of 0.01 to 20 V
The signal-generator wave names are sine, square, triangle, ramp_up, ramp_down and dc
set_signal_generator converts amplitude_v to peak-to-peak (amplitude * 2 * 1e6) and calls ps5000aSetSigGenBuiltInV2 with the frequency and wave
stop_signal_generator sets the generator to DC at 0 V to turn the output off
The README states that set_signal_generator and stop_signal_generator drive the built-in AWG with sine, square, triangle and ramp, frequency and amplitude
capture_block captures one block on all enabled channels and returns the sample count, sample interval, sample rate, duration, timebase and per-channel measurements
The per-channel analysis returns vpp_mv, vmin_mv, vmax_mv, mean_mv, rms_mv, frequency_hz, over_range and a downsampled waveform_mv
The README states that capture_block returns Vpp/min/max/mean/rms, an estimated frequency and a downsampled waveform
The capture waits up to 10 s for ps5000aIsReady and stops the unit when the deadline passes
The pyproject declares numpy and picosdk as runtime dependencies
